articles.title: US Open 2026 quarter-finals: Andreeva v Gauff, Rybakina beats Zheng to become world No 1 – live
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina beats Zheng Qinwen 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 Shelton advances after night of sweat and tears Get in touch: email Niall | Follow us on TikTok. Rybakina has won four of her five meetings with Zheng, including two three-set victories this year.
body: Andreeva opens with an ace, then Gauff tries to attack her second serve but only finds the net. The American prevails in the next rally, solid defence drawing an error – and Andreeva double-faults! A bit of pressure, but Gauff can’t keep her next return in play. Set point, secured with a big serve down the line.

At 30-15 up, Gauff serves up another dispiriting double fault – but Andreeva can’t quite keep her return in from a serve out wide. The next serve doesn’t come back, either. Still, Andreeva will have two chances to serve out the first set.
Andreeva holds in the blink of an eye to continue her domination of this first set. She’s never reached the quarter-finals here before, but looks much more comfortable than Gauff, the 2023 champion.
Coco Gauff gets on the board with a hold to 15, and at least has a foothold after producing 10 unforced errors to Andreeva’s two so far.

articles.title: Infantino installs loyalist to oversee Caribbean as he splits Fifa management
articles.summary: Critics view Fernandes job as move to shore up position. Fifa says change is designed to make sport ‘truly global’ Gianni Infantino has separated Fifa’s management of the Caribbean countries from the rest of Concacaf in a move widely regarded by his opponents as an attempt to split the alliance to…
body: Concacaf covers North and Central America as well as the Caribbean and was previously managed as one bloc. But the Guardian has learned that the former Switzerland midfielder Gelson Fernandes, an Infantino loyalist, has been appointed as the director of member associations for the Caribbean, in addition to his position looking after Fifa’s African members.

Fernandes, who played for Manchester City, Leicester and eight other clubs, joined Fifa in 2022 as director of member associations for Africa and was promoted two years later to become deputy chief members associations officer globally.
The 40-year-old works closely with Fifa’s chief members associations officer, Elkhan Mammadov, a close ally of Infantino described by many national associations as the president’s key enforcer.
Fernandes has replaced Jair Bertoni as Fifa’s liaison with the 21 Caribbean-based members, with the national associations and Concacaf informed of the change last week without consultation.

articles.title: Vuelta a España: Matthew ⁠Brennan rounds off famous five with sprint success
articles.summary: Young British rider squeezes out Meeus and Cort Nielsen. Mas moves step closer to landing first Grand Tour victory. Matthew Brennan claimed a fifth Vuelta a España stage victory on Wednesday as the young British rider edged a bunch sprint in Seville to win the 17th stage.
body: The general classification leader, Enric Mas, moved one step closer to claiming a first Grand Tour victory as he maintained his 2min 6sec lead on Felix Gall, with four-time Vuelta winner Primoz Roglic a further four seconds behind.
The stage was set up for the bunch sprint finale, without a single climb on the long, flat, 185km ride from Dos Hermanas to the Andalusian capital.

Sinuhe Fernandez and Enzo Paleni formed a two-man break early on, whipping up a gap of more than four minutes on the peloton, who were moving at a leisurely pace on another hot day with temperatures over 30C.

The gap extended to more than five minutes around the halfway point, with Visma then working hard to reduce it. The Groupama FDJ-United rider Paleni dropped Fernandez but was absorbed by the peloton with just three kilometres remaining after a monumental effort.

articles.title: Zaib hits century for Northants at New Road
articles.summary: Saif Zaib scores 110 as Northants take an 89-run first-innings lead against Worcestershire, who are 55-3 at the end of the second day's play.
body: Saif Zaib made a superb 110 before a late Harry Conway burst ripped through Worcestershire's top order to send Northamptonshire into pole position on day two of their County Championship game at New Road.

A second century of the summer from Zaib, supported by a controlled 52 from James Sales, saw the visitors establish an 89-run lead over Worcestershire, whose fightback was led by Matthew Waite's 3-31.
Bowled out for 289, seamer Conway ensured Northants took full control of the contest late in the day in a spell of 3-19.
The Pears closed 55-3, trailing by 34 runs in their second innings, as the promotion chasing visitors tightened their grip.

articles.title: England demolish Pakistan to take charge of Test
articles.summary: England again demolish the dismal Pakistan batting to move on course for a 3-0 clean sweep on the opening day of the third Test at Edgbaston.
body: After ripping out the tourists for only 133, England already have a 23-run advantage on 156-4.
Following a week of turmoil in which Pakistan sent seven players home, called up seven more and changed their coach, the outcome was much the same as the first two Tests.
Though the dry pitch seemed good for batting, a moody morning sky convinced England captain Joe Root to field first and his new-look pace attack was outstanding once more.

Pakistan failed to reach 200 for the fifth consecutive innings, while none of the top five made double figures. Saud Shakeel at least managed 43 and the ineptitude of the top order was put into context by last-wicket pair Muhammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali adding 26 in 46 balls - the best partnership of the innings.

articles.title: Lehmann's unbeaten ton for Hants frustrates Notts
articles.summary: Jake Lehmann's unbeaten 115 was the standout performance on day two of the County Championship Division One match between Nottinghamshire and Hampshire at Trent Bridge.
body: Only Lancashire have scored fewer runs per wicket lost than Hampshire's average of just 24.50. Yet Lehmann, their South Australian playing under a British passport, can boast the joint-second highest aggregate of runs (922) in the top tier.
Unsurprisingly, as their reply reached 267-7 at the close, 110 runs behind Notts, it was Lehmann who top-scored with a superb innings showing novel footwork, reminiscent of his father Darren.
Crucially he found a resolute partner in Scott Currie who resisted 143 balls for 35 to revive his side from 165-6 in a seventh-wicket stand of 97 that has kept Hampshire in the game.

Currie, with a single century to his credit two years ago when on loan to Leicestershire, helped leave Notts still needing two wickets from ten overs on day three if they are to take maximum bonus points and then seek the win.

articles.title: Gurney called up to World Series Finals after withdrawals due to visa issues
articles.summary: Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event.
body: Northern Ireland's Gurney and the Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list and have replaced Ilagan and Toylo respectively after the pair did not receive a decision on their Schengen visa applications before having to travel to China this week for the final two events of the PDC Asian Tour season.
Gurney will face reigning tournament champion and home favourite Michael van Gerwen in the first round at AFAS Live on Thursday September 17, while Kuivenhoven plays Jonny Clayton the following day.
Luke Littler, the 2024 champion who was beaten 11-7 by Van Gerwen in last year's final, heads to Amsterdam aiming to keep his bid for the first-ever clean sweep of majors in one year on track.
Luke Humphries opens against Jermaine Wattimena, while Gian van Veen will face Chris Dobey.

articles.summary: Raphinha continued his superb goalscoring form with a brace as Barcelona demolished Feyenoord 5-1 to begin their Champions League campaign in perfect fashion on Wednesday.
body: Karim Adeyemi curled home brilliantly from long range in between Raphinha's strikes and Lamine Yamal bent in a free-kick as Hansi Flick's team made light work of their Dutch visitors.
After Sem Steijn pulled one back, Barca substitute Gabriel Jesus netted a fifth, the forward's first goal since joining from Arsenal this summer.
The Catalan giants, who last won the competition in 2015, have triumphed in all five of their matches across all competitions this season -- and scored five goals in four of them.
Brazilian winger Raphinha has been playing up front after Barca sold Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and has rapidly taken to his new position, plundering eight goals in five games.

articles.title: Tongue tears through sorry Pakistan as England earn lead on day one
articles.summary: England dominated a sorry-looking Pakistan yet again on day one of the third Test at Edgbaston, bowling the tourists out for 133 before closing on 156-4, with a 23-run lead.
body: Emilio Gay (60) and Harry Brook (52no) each struck fifties in the final session to rescue England from 39-3 after their own top-order wobble, in which Joe Root (8) was pinned lbw for a 10th time in 13 innings by Pakistan's hugely-impressive debutant pacer Razaullah (2-42).

Root had earlier opted to insert the visitors at the toss in overcast conditions, but it wasn't long before his side were preparing to bat anyway, as Pakistan lasted just 33.5 overs - their shortest innings in a series full of disappointing batting displays.
Seven wickets fell in a chaotic morning session which saw Ollie Robinson (3-15) claim his 100th in Test cricket, before the innings was wrapped up soon after lunch.

Josh Tongue finished with 4-42, dismantling the stumps of Pakistan captain Babar Azam (7), Mohammad Imran (5) and lone bright spark Saud Shakeel (43), while Jofra Archer proved potent once more, taking 3-25.

articles.title: 'Chickens come home to roost' for PCB as 'dismal' batting costs Pakistan
articles.summary: It is not unreasonable to say that Pakistan entered the third Test of their three-match series against England with a dark cloud over them - off-field issues, coupled with the underwhelming on-field displays, combining to create the perfect storm.
body: "Unprecedented" was the word used by Sky Sports Cricket's Michael Atherton to describe the upheaval that has occurred over the last week in response to heavy losses at Headingley and Lords.
Seven players were sent home, head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul were replaced, and an investigation began into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct".
If those actions were aimed at provoking a response, the Pakistan Cricket Board did not get the one it would have been after on day one at Edgbaston.
On the eve of the third Test, Root dismissed suggestions that Pakistan have shown "no fight" in the series as disrespectful to both teams.
